repetition_detector_tuning.note: severe = one line is >=50% of the whole extracted proof and repeats >=4x; these are invisible to is_degenerate() because it only inspects the raw RESPONSE text (paragraphs >=40 chars), never the final extracted proof, and never lines shorter than 40 chars.

actionable_findings.description: extract_lemma_names() only matches capitalized dot-namespaced identifiers (regex requires [A-Z]...\....). 57.5% of real hallucinated names found in this corpus are plain lowercase snake_case (e.g. div_lt_div_iff, abs_add, pow_le_pow_right), so the autoformalizer's 'avoid these names' retry silently misses most real hallucinations.
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: broaden the regex to also match lowercase snake_case identifiers with a word-boundary guard against short local hypothesis names (h1, hx, etc.)

actionable_findings.description: _MIN_PARAGRAPH_LEN = 40 means any repeated unit shorter than 40 chars is invisible to is_degenerate(). Found 19 'severe' cases in the corpus where a short line (e.g. '#check False', '#eval (10 : ℚ) / 3', '\\end{cases}') makes up ~100% of the final proof (up to 4958 repeated lines), burning the full max_new_tokens budget uncaught.
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: add an independent short-line repetition check (any line >=8 chars repeated >=4x) alongside the existing paragraph check

actionable_findings.description: 33.8% of 'unknown identifier' errors are actually local variable scoping bugs (e.g. using `i`, `n`, `k` out of scope), not invented Mathlib lemma names, but has_hallucinated_lemma() triggers the autoformalizer rescue for both cases identically.
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: optionally filter to names that look lemma-shaped (contain '_' or '.', length > 3) before triggering the rescue path

actionable_findings.description: A small but distinct failure mode: the model references a local hypothesis (h_f1_0, h_f2_0, k.succ) it never actually introduced earlier in its own proof - a proof-planning/bookkeeping failure, not an API hallucination. Currently bucketed together with real hallucinations by has_hallucinated_lemma().
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: no fix required necessarily, but worth tracking separately in analysis since the root cause (and any future fix) differs from Mathlib-API hallucination

actionable_findings.description: On tier0 (MATH-sourced, easiest), the autoformalizer rescued 4/191 attempts (~2%) contributing 4/80 completes. On the mintier1 (AMC/AIME/IMO) batch, the autoformalizer rescued 0/29 attempts, contributing 0 completes in the 33-problem checkpoint analyzed.
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: n/a - basis for the decision to drop the autoformalizer for the harder mintier1 run

lean_verification.method: LeanServer.identifier_exists() against the live Mathlib v4.25.2 install (#check <name>, checking for zero error-severity messages)

sanity_check.note: abs_add was included as a 'known real' sanity check and SURPRISINGLY returned False - confirmed genuinely absent as a bare identifier in this Mathlib version, not a checker bug (the other 4 controls + a deliberately-fake control name all behaved as expected).

lean_verification.correction_to_earlier_hedge: The 'likely_real_but_misused_context' bucket in hallucination_taxonomy (abs_add, Complex.abs, Complex.sq_abs, Nat.dvd_sub', Nat.odd_iff_not_even) was a HEDGED GUESS based on training-knowledge pattern-matching, explicitly flagged as unverified at the time. Live verification against the actual Mathlib v4.25.2 install shows ALL of these are confirmed fabrications (identifier_exists() == False), same as everything else in the corpus. There is no 'misused-but-real' subset - 100% of the 81 checked hallucinated-lemma-shaped names are genuine fabrications in this Mathlib version. The hallucination_taxonomy category names/groupings by naming-convention pattern (false_memory_repeat, lean3_vintage_or_renamed, etc.) still stand as a classification of WHY each name looks the way it does, but none of them should be read as 'this one might actually work'.
